newsitem.title: USA: BPA buys power as hydropower dams fill for fish.
newsitem.headline: BPA buys power as hydropower dams fill for fish.

text.p: The Portland, Oregon-based Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) purchased power in the real-time as well as pre-scheduled markets and may continue to buy through the end of the week, market sources said Tuesday.
"We are trying to get the system full by the end of July," said a BPA trader.
"We definitely wouldn't be doing this now if we didn't have to," he added.
Environmentalists and fish watchers have called for regional reservoir levels to be at target levels so that enough water will be available for fish flows next month, sources said.
"They want to make sure we have the maximum level on hand for August," said another BPA source.
With regional streamflows slightly lower than expected, BPA is buying back some of the power it sold forward this month now that dam discharges are being curtailed.
BPA said the Grand Coulee dam on the Columbia River in Washington state needs to be filled by another 2 feet or so by August 3.
"Until now, natural flows have been enough to meet targets, but we expect the fish people to start requiring the maximum on August 4," the BPA trader said.
In addition, work to repair damaged fish ladders at the Bonneville Dam in Oregon has cut capacity at the dam by about 200 MW.

The repair work is expected to last as long as four months, but BPA hopes to be able to restart the idled turbines after the end of August, when gas bubble limitations, also related to fish migration, will expire.
